title: Adaptive baseline drift mitigation for PR gating using reservoir sampling + multi-window smoothing
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: CI PR gating occasionally produces false positive performance regressions due to short-term workload variance and outlier microbursts. Current single-window baselines drift or overreact to transient bursts, causing noisy gate failures and developer overhead.

Goal: Implement an adaptive baseline mitigation layer that stabilizes PR gating decisions by combining reservoir-sampled historic exemplars with multi-window smoothing (fast/medium/slow windows). The system should reduce false positives at p95 and tokens/sec gates by 60% in noisy workloads while still detecting true regressions within one PR iteration for sustained degradations.

Scope: server-side CI harness components, baseline maintenance job, gating decision delta logic, telemetry dashboards, and automated backfill for existing baseline data. Not in scope: changes to downstream on-call escalation workflows (will be handled in follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: New baseline service emits stable baseline metrics for every benchmark job with three window aggregates (fast/medium/slow)
PR gating policy uses ensemble decision: require sustained deviation across at least two windows OR a combined z-score threshold to fail a gate
False positive rate on historical noisy traces reduced >= 60% compared to current single-window baseline (measured on last 6 months of CI runs)
Alerting and dashboard surfaces per-job drift score and rationale for failed gates
Canary rollout on CI: default OFF for mainline runs, ON for trusted repo subset; roll forward plan and kill-switch documented
design_notes: Reservoir sampling for historical exemplar retention: keep N=1000 samples per job across a long window (90 days) to avoid skew from recent bursts
Maintain three EWMA-like aggregates: fast (~1h), medium (~24h), slow (~14d) with configurable half-lives; use median-of-samples inside each window to resist outliers
Decision rule: compute normalized delta per metric (tokens/sec, p95 latency) against each window; gate fail if either (a) medium+slow both exceed threshold OR (b) combined ensemble z-score > 4.0
Compute uncertainty band using bootstrap on sample reservoir to estimate p95 variance; widen gate threshold under high-uncertainty
Backfill strategy: seed reservoir with compressed historic runs from cold storage; run a one-off reconciliation job to compute initial aggregates
Keep gating deterministic: use locked seed for reservoir tie-breakers so CI decisions are reproducible for a given dataset
implementation_plan: 1) Baseline service: new lightweight API (read-only for CI) that serves per-job reservoirs and window aggregates
2) Reservoir maintainer: streaming consumer of CI job events that updates job reservoirs and recomputes aggregates incrementally
3) PR gating change: update GitHub PR gate runner to query baseline service and apply ensemble rules; provide verbose failure reason when gate fails
4) Telemetry: emit drift_score, window_deltas, reservoir_size, and uncertainty to existing observability pipeline (Tracing/Prometheus/Logs)
5) Backfill: one-time Spark/beam job to populate reservoirs from archived benchmark traces
6) Canary rollout: enable for perf-team repos -> expand to self-serve opt-in for other teams -> global default on after stability window
7) Post-launch: run A/B study comparing gate outcomes (false positives/negatives) and adjust thresholds accordingly
test_plan: Unit tests for reservoir sampling invariants and aggregate computation
Synthetic replay harness: inject controlled microburst sequences and steady degradations to validate decision sensitivity
Ground-truth run: replay last 6 months of CI benchmark logs and compare current gate results vs new ensemble gate with metrics (TP/FP/FN/TN)
Canary PRs: open curated PRs with synthetic regressions to verify detection latency and rationale messages
Load test baseline service for read QPS during peak CI hours (target 5000rps for GitHub PR matrix) with p95 < 50ms for queries
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Reservoir storage growth. Mitigation: TTL + reservoir cap + probabilistic compaction job.
Risk: Increased gate complexity leads to developer confusion. Mitigation: verbose failure rationale, docs, and rollout opt-in for teams.
Risk: Delayed detection of slow regressions if thresholds too lax. Mitigation: require at least two-window agreement OR chained alerts to oncall on slow-window drift.
Risk: Canary false negatives. Mitigation: parallel dry-run mode that logs decisions without failing PRs for 2 weeks before enforcing.
dependencies: ENG-4821 (CI performance metrics standardization) - alignment required for metric names
Infra: object store access for backfill (S3 path: s3://redwood-ci/bench-archive)
Observability team: add drift_score to metrics schema
Security review: ensure reservoir blobs contain no PII (bench input sanitized)
